BEFORE THE GEORGIA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

Georgia Power Company
Docket No. 56002
2025 Integrated Resource Plan

BASIS FOR THE ASSERTION THAT THE
INFORMATION SUBMITTED IS A TRADE SECRET

In accordance with the Order Adopting Stipulation issued by the Georgia Public Service
Commission (“Commission”) in Docket Nos. 56002 and 56003 on July 31, 2025, Georgia Power
Company (“Georgia Power” or the “Company” is filing its Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report for
the period ending June 30, 2026. The report contains proprietary cost and schedule data (the
“Information”). All such Information constitutes trade secret Information of the Southern Company,
Georgia Power, and its affiliates and is therefore protected from public disclosure under Commission
Rule 515-3-1-.11.

The Information derives economic value from not being generally known to and not being
readily ascertainable by proper means by other persons who can obtain economic value from its
disclosure or use. Specifically, the trade secret portions of the Information include confidential
budgetary and schedule information related to nuclear uprate projects. Public dissemination of the
Information would allow Georgia Power’s potential suppliers and contractors access to such
estimated costs and timelines, thereby bestowing insight into the Company’s budgeted cost and
timing of such expenditures. Such access would grant an unfair advantage to contractors and
suppliers of the Company, who could use such information to artificially set bid and proposal
prices during contract negotiations. This could lead to the Company having to pay a price higher
than that which it would have paid on a level playing field.

The Information is subject to substantial procedures to maintain its secrecy. Only select
Georgia Power and Southern Company Services personnel are granted access to the Information.
Those personnel receive access only on a “need to know” basis. Parties outside the Company who
have been granted access to the Information, if any, have been required to sign confidentiality
agreements with respect to the Information.

 Jeffrey R. Grubb, first being duly swom, deposes and states that he has reviewed Georgia
Power Company’s Information in the above-styled Dockets to that the information included is
accurate to the best of his knowledge and that the specific information designated as trade secret
constitute trade secrets pursuant to Article 27 of Chapter 1 of Title 10 of the Official Code of
Georgia.

Georgia Power Company

Subscribed and sworn to before me this. 1 day of September 2026.

Georgia Power Company’s 
Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report



Reporting Period End Date: June 30, 2026








Project Background
This Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report (“Report”) provides the status of the Extended Power Uprates (“EPUs”) at Plant Vogtle Units 1-2 (“Plant Vogtle”) and Plant Hatch Units 1-2 (“Plant Hatch”). This Report is filed pursuant to the Georgia Public Service Commission’s (the “Commission”) Order Adopting Stipulation, dated July 31, 2025 (the “Order”) in Georgia Power Company’s (“Georgia Power” or the “Company”) 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (“2025 IRP”), Docket No. 56002.  

EPU is a validated, proven process that has been implemented previously at Plant Hatch and Plant Vogtle, and by other nuclear electric utility operators, that delivers incremental capacity and energy gains. The objective of the EPU process is to increase thermal power (where the reactor produces more heat) to increase steam pressure and flow to the turbine generators, thus producing higher electrical output from the units without using additional fuel. The process includes an extensive analysis of plant systems and components to verify the capability of the EPUs and identify the modifications needed to support the power upgrade at each facility. 

The EPU projects will modify key components of the units, including turbines, generators, large pumps and motors, and cooling systems, to allow the units to safely and reliably produce more electricity. Many of the modifications will replace existing components that are contemplated for future end-of-life replacement to enhance performance, and some will create incremental capacity gains from the increased thermal output of the EPU implementation. The Company identifies components as end-of-life when the component is expected to be replaced within the expected operating life of the plant. The EPU components include:

Turbine Upgrade: The high-pressure (“HP”) turbine will be upgraded to handle the increased steam flow and pressure. HP turbines are the first to receive steam and experience the highest temperatures and pressures. 
Steam Cycle Upgrades:
Feedwater Heaters: (Hatch only) Preheat water entering the reactor, which improves efficiency of the water heating process in the reactor.
Moisture Separator Reheaters (MSRs): (Vogtle Units 1-2 only) Remove water droplets from the steam and reheat the steam before it enters the Low-pressure turbines, thus protecting the turbines and improving efficiency.
Steam Dryers: (Hatch only) Remove moisture from the steam, like MSRs. Upgrading steam dryers ensures high steam quality and improves turbine efficiency and reliability under increased steam flow conditions.
Condensate Pumps and Motors: (Hatch only) Move condensed steam from the condenser to the feedwater system. Upgrading will improve efficiency and ensure proper flows and pressures for the feedwater system.
Cooling Tower / Circulating Water: Provides an energy efficient way of removing heat from water that circulates through the condenser. Adding cooling towers, replacing fill material, and/or upgrading circulating water pumps will accommodate additional steam produced after the EPUs.
Generator Upgrade: The generator will be upgraded to handle the increased power output. Upgrades to the exciter and/or rotor are needed for increased generation.
Maximum Extended Load Line Limit Analysis Plus (MELLLA+): (Hatch Only) Expands the power/flow map to provide more operating flexibility for uprated plants to achieve full core thermal power.

Key Updates (January 1, 2026 – June 30, 2026)
General Progress Update
Schedule development for EPU project implementation continued to make significant progress through the year. This progress has developed further confidence and reduced risk in the ability to complete the engineering analysis, licensing, and implementation periods as designed. 
Plant Vogtle Units 1-2
Engineering Status
Westinghouse Engineering (“Westinghouse”) analysis Step 1, Feasibility Engineering Analysis, was initiated April 2024 and completed October 2024. Step 2 of 3, Preliminary Engineering Study of the incremental capacity uprate, commenced with Westinghouse in November 2024 and concluded in March 2026. This phase further refined the project scope that supports the uprate.  SNC received the proposal from Westinghouse for the final Step 3 Engineering and Licensing phase and anticipates executing the contract in the third quarter of 2026. Major contracts are included in Attachment 1.
Transmission and interconnection activities continued during the reporting period to support the Plant Vogtle Units 1-2 EPU project. Southern Nuclear, Georgia Power, and Transmission Services personnel completed the Cluster Study, Generator Interconnection and Power Delivery reviews, and Affected System Study activities. These studies evaluated Plant Vogtle’s incremental generation and its impact on generator interconnection and delivery such as reactive power requirements, short circuit and breaker duty analysis, stability analysis, protection requirements, interface capabilities, nuclear offsite power, and impacted facilities. By June 2026, the transmission planning study indicated that sufficient information had been provided to support continuation of the generator interconnection and affected system process, and no additional requests for study information were pending at that time. Current transmission evaluations have not identified any material transmission limitations that would alter the planned project development path, and coordination with affected transmission providers remains ongoing as engineering, licensing, and implementation activities progress.
During the reporting period, Southern Nuclear Company continued developing the licensing strategy and supporting analyses for the Plant Vogtle Units 1-2 Extended Power Uprate. The Preliminary Engineering Study was completed in March 2026 and planning advanced for the next phase of engineering analysis and License Amendment Request (“LAR”) development. The licensing strategy coordinates the EPU request with related fuel-transition, spent fuel pool criticality, safety-analysis methodology, and potential longer-term fuel-cycle licensing activities.
Work also continued on the fuel-transition licensing package and the supporting analyses necessary to demonstrate operation under the proposed fuel and uprated conditions. These activities include fuel engineering, development of the full-spectrum loss-of-coolant accident evaluation model, spent fuel pool criticality analysis, and preparation of associated licensing-basis changes. Where appropriate, SNC is evaluating opportunities to coordinate or bound related analyses to reduce duplicative work while maintaining the necessary technical and regulatory support for each licensing action.
Following completion of the next engineering and licensing phase, SNC currently projects completion of the principal EPU supporting analyses no later than the first quarter of 2029 and submission of the EPU LAR no later than the second quarter of 2029. The current project schedule projects completion of the NRC’s EPU review and approval no later than the third quarter of 2030.
Longer-term licensing activities include NRC review of the EPU request and coordination with related initiatives involving higher-enrichment fuel, higher burnup, advanced fuel methodologies, and potential operation on a 24-month fuel cycle. These related actions will continue to be refined as engineering progresses and NRC review expectations are further developed. The NRC controls changes to a plant’s licensed maximum power level and Technical Specifications, and an uprate may not be implemented until the NRC approves the applicable license amendment. 
The present project timeline anticipates implementation of the Vogtle EPU over the 2030-2031 period. Because engineering and licensing development remain underway, these longer-term projections may be refined as the technical scope, licensing strategy, NRC review schedule, and related project dependencies mature.
A detailed licensing and implementation schedule for the Vogtle Units 1-2 EPU Project can be found in Attachment 3.
Efficiency Projections
As reported in the 12/31/2025 Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report, the vendor provided updated efficiency projections that ranged from 23-24 MWe per unit (GPC 46.8% ownership), representing a 13.0% decrease from what was initially projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. During the engineering analysis, an issue was identified with increasing the temperature of the reactor coolant system that would present a long-term vulnerability to the Steam Generators. Accordingly, it was determined to target a lower temperature increase to mitigate that risk. The lower temperature target results in lower total MWe gains per unit.  
As of June 30, 2026, the Company has no update for the incremental capacity gains. It will conclude the independent assessment of the MWe gains in September. The final range for the Vogtle 1-2 uprate projection is assumed to be approximately 21-24 MWe per unit (GPC 46.8% ownership), representing up to a 16% decrease from what was initially projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan.  
Near Term Projects Status:

The Moisture Separator Reheaters and Heater Drain motors engineering designs are in progress and on track to support implementation as noted above. The procurement of these components with the applicable vendors is on track and delivery of the components to the site is projected to meet the above schedule for implementation.
Near-term licensing activities will focus on continued development of the fuel-transition LAR and the spent fuel pool criticality LAR. The current schedule targets submission of the fuel-transition LAR in the third quarter of 2027. The licensing schedule currently contemplates submitting the spent fuel pool criticality LAR shortly before the fuel-transition LAR, although SNC is evaluating whether that submittal can be advanced. Updates to supporting licensing documents, including the Technical Requirements Manual, Final Safety Analysis Report, and Core Operating Limits Report, are scheduled for completion during the fourth quarter of 2027.
Project Scope 
Southern Nuclear Company (“SNC”) completed the factory acceptance testing to evaluate the upgraded rating of the step-up transformers associated with the uprate project in June. Testing  concluded a success path, and the project continues to meet the cost portfolio.
Financial Update 
The total capital cost estimate remains approximately $████ million. Details through June 30, 2026 are provided in the table below.

Plant Hatch Units 1-2
Engineering Status
Engineering analysis for the incremental capacity uprates began with GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy in August 2025 and remains on schedule for completion on or before October 2027. This phase confirms the scope and prepares the documentation for the LAR. Contract status details are provided in Attachment 2.
Transmission planning activities for the Plant Hatch Units 1-2 EPU project also progressed during the reporting period. Southern Nuclear, Georgia Power, and Transmission Services personnel completed the Cluster Study, Generator Interconnection and Power Delivery reviews, and the Affected System Study activities. These studies evaluated Plant Hatch’s proposed incremental generation and its impact on generator interconnection and delivery such as reactive power requirements, short circuit and breaker duty analysis, stability analysis, protection requirements, interface capabilities, nuclear offsite power, and impacted facilities. By June 2026, the transmission planning study indicated that sufficient information had been provided to support continuation of the generator interconnection and affected system process, and no additional study information requests were pending at that time. Current transmission evaluations have not identified any material transmission limitations that would alter the planned project development path, and coordination with affected transmission providers remains ongoing as engineering and licensing activities progress.
During the reporting period, SNC continued engineering and licensing development for the Plant Hatch Units 1-2 EPU. Current activities include development of the combined EPU and MELLLA+ licensing strategy, preparation of the associated safety analysis report, and advancement of the technical analyses needed to support the LAR. The licensing approach also considers related Alternative Source Term, reactor protection, and subsequent license renewal activities.
The current timeline reflects continued coordination among engineering, licensing, project planning, and vendor activities. This work is intended to define the analyses and licensing-basis changes necessary to demonstrate safe operation at the proposed uprated conditions and under the expanded operating flexibility provided by MELLLA+.
The present project timeline anticipates implementation of the Hatch Units 1-2 EPU over the 2030-2031 period. Because engineering and licensing development remain underway, these longer-term projections may be refined as the technical scope, licensing strategy, NRC review schedule, and related project dependencies mature.
A detailed licensing and implementation schedule for the Hatch Units 1-2 EPU Project can be found in Attachment 3.
Efficiency Projections
As reported in the 12/31/2025 Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report, projected efficiency gains from the upgraded HP turbines are slightly below earlier estimates and now range from 23-26 MWe per unit (GPC 50.1% ownership), representing a 15.7% decrease from what was initially projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. Heat balance analyses to validate these assumptions are underway and scheduled for completion in March 2026. 
Since the prior report, SNC completed an independent third-party evaluation of the Hatch EPU generation uplift and received updated heat-balance analyses from GE Vernova. As engineering analysis progressed, the expected conversion efficiency associated with the uprate was refined from approximately 34% to approximately 31%, resulting in lower expected generation gains than originally assumed in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. The independent evaluation developed a probabilistic distribution of expected capacity gains and identified several confidence-based outcomes. The analysis estimated a total generation increase of approximately 45.4 MWe total at the 95% confidence level, representing a highly conservative outcome with a high degree of certainty, while the likely outcome was estimated at approximately 56.9 MWe at the 75% confidence level total for both units (GPC 50.1% ownership). Higher generation gains were also identified within the distribution under more favorable operating and performance conditions. These results provide a quantitative framework for evaluating expected project performance and support continued refinement of the Company's capacity projections. Based on the GE Vernova analyses and the independent evaluation, SNC continues to advance engineering, economic, and licensing activities using the updated performance expectations developed through these analyses.



Near Term Projects Status:

The engineering design projects are in progress and on track to support implementation, as noted above. The procurement of these components with the applicable vendors is on track and delivery of the components to the site is projected to meet the above schedule for implementation.
Near-term efforts will focus on completing the engineering and safety analyses supporting the combined EPU/MELLLA+ application and developing the associated LAR documentation. The existing report schedule anticipates completing the supporting engineering analysis in 2027 and submission of the LAR during the third quarter of 2027. 
SNC will also continue coordinating the EPU/MELLLA+ licensing package with other Hatch licensing activities, including the ongoing Alternative Source Term review and subsequent license renewal.
Following submission, the current schedule projects completion of the NRC’s EPU/MELLLA+ review and approval during the second quarter of 2028. 
Project Scope
As reported in the 12/31/2025 Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report, SNC and vendor analysis of the HP Turbine and 4th Stage Feedwater Heaters identified that the existing components are degraded beyond Company management margin expectations and require replacement within the next several years. Accordingly, the Company has decided to move forward with procuring these assets for implementation during upcoming refueling outages. The HP Turbine has been moved to the general plant-in-service budget to continue implementation for plant reliability purposes. There have been no additional modifications to report since the prior report.
Financial Update
The total capital cost estimate remains approximately $███ million. Details through June 30, 2026 are provided in the table below.

1. Engineering Status

Engineering analysis for the incremental capacity uprates began with GE Vernova Hitachi
Nuclear Energy in August 2025 and remains on schedule for completion on or before October
2027. This phase confirms the scope and prepares the documentation for the LAR. Contract
status details are provided in Attachment 2.

Transmission planning activities for the Plant Hatch Units 1-2 EPU project also progressed
during the reporting period. Southern Nuclear, Georgia Power, and Transmission Services
personnel completed the Cluster Study, Generator Interconnection and Power Delivery reviews,
and the Affected System Study activities. These studies evaluated Plant Hatch’s proposed
incremental generation and its impact on generator interconnection and delivery such as reactive
power requirements, short circuit and breaker duty analysis, stability analysis, protection
requirements, interface capabilities, nuclear offsite power, and impacted facilities. By June 2026,
the transmission planning study indicated that sufficient information had been provided to
support continuation of the generator interconnection and affected system process, and no
additional study information requests were pending at that time. Current transmission evaluations
have not identified any material transmission limitations that would alter the planned project
development path, and coordination with affected transmission providers remains ongoing as
engineering and licensing activities progress.
During the reporting period, SNC continued engineering and licensing development for the Plant
Hatch Units 1-2 EPU. Current activities include development of the combined EPU and

advancement of the technical analyses needed to support the LAR. The licensing approach also

2. Efficiency Projections

As reported in the 12/31/2025 Semi-Annual Nuclear Uprate Report, projected efficiency gains
from the upgraded HP turbines are slightly below earlier estimates and now range from 23-26
MWe per unit (GPC 50.1% ownership), representing a 15.7% decrease from what was initially
projected in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. Heat balance analyses to validate
these assumptions are underway and scheduled for completion in March 2026.

Since the prior report, SNC completed an independent third-party evaluation of the Hatch EPU
generation uplift and received updated heat-balance analyses from GE Vernova. As engineering
analysis progressed, the expected conversion efficiency associated with the uprate was refined
from approximately 34% to approximately 31%, resulting in lower expected generation gains
than originally assumed in the Company’s 2025 Integrated Resource Plan. The independent
evaluation developed a probabilistic distribution of expected capacity gains and identified
several confidence-based outcomes. The analysis estimated a total generation increase of
approximately 45.4 MWe total at the 95% confidence level, representing a highly conservative
outcome with a high degree of certainty, while the likely outcome was estimated at
approximately 56.9 MWe at the 75% confidence level total for both units (GPC 50.1%
ownership). Higher generation gains were also identified within the distribution under more
favorable operating and performance conditions. These results provide a quantitative framework
for evaluating expected project performance and support continued refinement of the Company's
capacity projections. Based on the GE Vernova analyses and the independent evaluation, SNC
continues to advance engineering, economic, and licensing activities using the updated
performance expectations developed through these analyses.
